findings.title: Light-theme color for embedded post author link changed from 30% to 70% lightness
findings.body: `.embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a` previously resolved to `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The new value is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`, so on light themes the author link is now scaled 70% toward white instead of 30%. Every other conversion in this PR preserves the original light value and uses its complement for the dark branch (e.g. 30%/70%). This silently reduces contrast of the author name in embedded/in-reply-to expansions on all existing light themes; the arguments appear to be swapped and should be `(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.

findings.title: Mobile topic-map h3 light-theme lightness changed from 20% to 50%
findings.body: `.topic-map h3` was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` and is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The light-theme value changed from 20% to 50% lightness, noticeably washing out the topic-map heading on mobile light themes, and it no longer matches the desktop rule which keeps 20%/80% (`desktop/topic-post.scss` line 321). The light branch should stay at 20% with an 80% dark complement.

findings.title: mobile .custom-message-length light/dark arguments are inverted
findings.body: `.custom-message-length` was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` and becomes `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. The light-theme value flipped from 70% to 30%, making the hint text much darker than before on mobile light themes, and it contradicts the desktop rule for the same class (`desktop/modal.scss` line 94) which uses 70%/30%. The arguments look swapped.

findings.title: group-member-info .name light value changed from 30% to 50%
findings.body: `.user-stream .group-member-info .name` was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` and is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The light-theme value changed from 30% to 50%, so the member name becomes lighter/lower-contrast than before and now renders identically to the adjacent `.title` (previously the name was intentionally darker than the title). Preserve 30% for the light branch with a 70% dark complement.

findings.title: mobile group-member-info .name light value changed from 30% to 50%
findings.body: Same regression as the desktop file: `.user-stream .group-member-info .name` was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` and is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The light-theme rendering changes (lighter text, no longer distinguishable from `.title` just below it, which uses the same 50%/50% pair). The light branch should remain 30%.

findings.title: #file-uploading color left as scale-color($secondary) and is invisible on light themes
findings.body: `#reply-control #file-uploading { color: scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%); }` was not converted. On a light theme `$secondary` is the (near-white) background color, so scaling it 50% toward white yields text that is effectively invisible against the composer background. Since this PR is specifically normalizing `scale-color()` usages for dark/light themes, this one should also become a `dark-light-choose(...)` pair based on `$primary` for light themes.

findings.title: Comment still documents the old scale-color($primary) default
findings.body: The comment above the coldmap rules states "the default for table cells in topic list is scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)", but the topic-list cell color was changed in this PR (`common/base/_topic-list.scss`) to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The comment is now misleading for anyone tuning these heat/cold map colors.
